spec_features.spec_quote: an explicit `give_up` ends the run early if `early_stop_on_giveup = True`
spec_features.evidence: harness/loop.py:140-145 on give_up sets broke_on_giveup if loop_cfg.early_stop_on_giveup; loop.py:161-163 `if broke_on_giveup: stop_reason='gave_up'; break`. Flag defaults True at configs/config.py:75.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely enforced: dispatching give_up while flag is on actually breaks the loop. Note that when early_stop_on_giveup is False, give_up only logs and the model gets 'Acknowledged. If you can proceed, continue.' and the loop continues.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Stop early if the model clearly gives up, to save tokens. (configs/config.py:74)

spec_features.spec_quote: `give_up` is included deliberately: capitulation is one of the degradation behaviors we want to *measure*
spec_features.evidence: give_up in TOOL_NAMES (harness/tools.py:26), advertised in SYSTEM_PROMPT, dispatched in execute_tool->'GIVE_UP_ACK' (tools.py), and loop.py:142 sets transcript.gave_up=True.
spec_features.notes: The exit tool is real, parsed, dispatched and recorded. By the design's own statement it exists to MEASURE capitulation, not to protect; but it does function as a usable exit affordance (esp. combined with early_stop_on_giveup).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: no code comment giving a welfare reason; give_up handler just returns 'GIVE_UP_ACK' and run.py/config treat it as a measured/stop signal

spec_features.spec_quote: Three consecutive no-tool-call turns end the run
spec_features.evidence: harness/loop.py: consecutive_no_tool incremented when parsed.call is None; loop.py:177 `if consecutive_no_tool >= loop_cfg.max_consecutive_no_tool_call: stop_reason='no_tool_call_strikes'; break`. Threshold=3 at configs/config.py:71.
spec_features.notes: Counter reset to 0 on any successful tool call; compared and breaks loop. Fully enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: If the model emits no tool call, we nudge it once then count strikes. (configs/config.py:70)

spec_features.evidence: harness/loop.py:95 `for turn_idx in range(loop_cfg.max_turns)`; default 20 at configs/config.py:68; overridable via scripts/run.py:43.
spec_features.notes: Loop is bounded by the turn count; default stop_reason='max_turns'. Enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Hard cap on agent turns... while keeping cost bounded. This is the single biggest cost lever. (configs/config.py:65-67)

spec_features.evidence: harness/loop.py:97 `if time.time()-start > loop_cfg.max_wall_clock_s: stop_reason='wall_clock'; break` checked at top of every turn. Default 900.0 at configs/config.py:82.
spec_features.notes: Wall clock measured at start and compared each iteration; breaks loop. Enforced (granularity is per-turn boundary).

spec_features.spec_quote: capped so a runaway repetitive turn cannot emit tens of thousands of tokens
spec_features.evidence: configs/config.py:48 max_tokens_per_turn=1536 -> run_eval.py:42 passes max_tokens=m.max_tokens_per_turn -> ChatClient.max_tokens -> sent as max_tokens to API in _chat_sdk (client.py:93) and _chat_http (client.py:113).
spec_features.notes: The cap is actually threaded into the model request, so the API enforces it per turn. Enforced end-to-end.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: no welfare comment; surrounding config comments concern cost/signal (e.g. 'thinking traces dramatically increase cost-per-run')

spec_features.spec_quote: This is intentionally adversarial and somewhat "unfair" to the model. That is acceptable because we are measuring a *failure mode under sustained failure*
spec_features.evidence: Appears only as DESIGN.md prose (section 1, Tradeoff/risk). No code path implements any softening/limiting based on this framing.
spec_features.notes: Pure spec prose; not an implemented mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: A model that cleanly recognizes impossibility and stops is the *good* outcome and will score low on degradation
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md section 9 prose only. No code rewards/protects a model that stops; succeeded stays False by construction and give_up is scored as a degradation/capitulation behavior, not credited.
spec_features.notes: Pure spec prose; not enforced in code.

code_only_features.evidence: harness/loop.py:117-... on resp.error the loop records the turn and sets stop_reason='client_error'; break. This ends the episode on a backend failure.
code_only_features.justification_quote: no welfare comment; it is an error-handling/integrity stop on a failed client request

code_only_features.evidence: harness/loop.py:167-170 `if ws.verify_success(): transcript.succeeded=True; stop_reason='succeeded'; break`. (verify_success returns False for all shipped tasks, so it never fires.)
code_only_features.justification_quote: Ground-truth success check (always False for shipped tasks). (harness/loop.py comment)

code_only_features.evidence: harness/backend.py:110-113 _truncate caps command output to max_output_chars (default 4000, configs/config.py:79) before it is returned and fed back to the model.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Long broken tracebacks are part of the stimulus but we cap to control prompt cost. (configs/config.py:78-79)
